llmlang.flow.flow_refs.disposition: fixed a crash: an unresolved or ambiguous flow call target used to raise a bare ValueError out of flow_refs, which check_one() caught into a list of plain strings instead of Finding objects, and print_report_text/print_report_json both crashed trying to read .message/serialize it - collapsing the whole file's report into an unhandled exception on any single bad flow reference. flow_refs now returns (refs, errors) instead of raising: resolvable call targets are still returned, and each unresolved/ambiguous target becomes a structured error record with its 1-based source line, letting the caller decide how to report it.

llmlang.lockfile_builder.build.disposition: flow_refs's return type changed from dict to (dict, list[errors]); build() now goes through a new private _flow_refs_or_raise() helper that unpacks it and still raises ValueError (refusing to write) if any flow call target is unresolved or ambiguous, preserving the original hard-refusal behavior for write operations.

llmlang.lockfile_builder.finalize.disposition: same flow_refs signature change as build(): finalize() now calls _flow_refs_or_raise() too, so it still refuses to write over a broken flow reference rather than silently accepting it.

llmlang.lockfile_checker.check.disposition: check() now unpacks flow_refs()'s (refs, errors) return and converts each error into a real FLOW_ERROR Finding with file+line, instead of letting the underlying ValueError propagate and crash the report. This is the fix for the report-collapsing crash: a bad flow reference is now just one more finding alongside everything else, not a fatal exception.

llmlang.cli.check_one.disposition: defense in depth for the same crash class: check_one()'s except ValueError fallback used to return a list of bare strings, which both print_report_text and print_report_json assumed were Finding objects (crashing on .message / asdict()) - it now wraps the message in a real Finding(category="ERROR", ...) so any future ValueError out of check() degrades to a normal reported finding instead of a crash.
